en.title: Polite expressions
en.summary: The small words that make English polite.

paragraphs: Politeness in English comes from small words and from the form of a request. A customer talks to a shop assistant.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Excuse me. Could I have a bottle of water, please?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Thank you. How much is it?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Sorry, could you repeat that, please?

paragraphs: **1. Could and would make a request polite.** Could I have...? and Could you...? are more polite than I want... or Give me... Add please at the beginning or the end. See Introduction to Grammar: Moods, command, subjunctive and conditional.

blocks.html:
Less politePolite
Give me water.Could I have some water, please?
Tell me the time.Could you tell me the time, please?

paragraphs: **2. Short words open and close a request.** Excuse me gets attention, please asks, thank you answers and sorry apologises. Add certainly or of course to agree. See Introduction to Grammar: Categories of words.

blocks.html:
WordUse
Excuse me.to get attention
Please.to ask
Thank you.to thank
Pardon?to ask for repetition

items: **Sorry?** and **Pardon?** both ask a person to repeat. **What?** is rude.
**Cheers** is an informal British word for thank you.
A request without please can sound abrupt, even with a friend.

paragraphs: English speakers use please and thank you much more than speakers of many other languages. Leaving them out can seem cold.
